j5-rrf-fusion-ablation.notes: LoCoMo 10 conversations, 1986 questions, NO_GATING, sha256-pinned corpus 79fa87e90f04081343b8c8debecb80a9a6842b76a7aa537dc9fdf651ea698ff4. Candidate pool = top-150 returned by retrieve() under the store default score; all arms re-rank the SAME pool so the comparison isolates the combination rule. Harness self-check: current 0.0906 / sim-only 0.3580 / no-recency 0.3046 reproduce diag-weight-ablation bit-exactly. LIMITATIONS: (1) this is an OFFLINE re-rank over a top-150 pool, NOT store-end-to-end retrievalScoreMode='rrf' over the full pool; a separate end-to-end run is required before citing these as the end-to-end figure. (2) MRR/NDCG conventions are defined locally in eval/j5-rrf-ablation.ts and are not cross-checkable against any existing repo baseline. (3) artifact provenance gitSha records 13fd0ce (HEAD at run time, before the RRF commit 55d692a). Code: feat(memory-biomimetic) 55d692a, opt-in, DEFAULT scoring mode unchanged.

j5-e2e-causal-decomposition.notes: LoCoMo 10 conversations, 1986 questions, NO_GATING, corpus sha256 79fa87e90f04081343b8c8debecb80a9a6842b76a7aa537dc9fdf651ea698ff4. Delivery track: full pool, retrieval noise and conflict penalty applied. Harness self-check: recall implementation agrees with eval-metrics.measure to 0.000000 (bit-identical). MEASURED 2x2, ALL FOUR CELLS: additive+no-dedupe 0.0836, additive+dedupe 0.0821, standardized+no-dedupe 0.1999, standardized+dedupe 0.2064. MAIN EFFECTS: score mode contributes +0.1163 (dedupe off) and +0.1244 (dedupe on); dedupe contributes -0.0015 (under additive) and +0.0065 (under standardized). INTERACTION (difference of differences) = +0.0081, i.e. 6.9% of the score-mode main effect -- small but of the same sign as predicted (dedupe helps only once scores are commensurable), and NOT established as significant at n=1986 without a paired test. The repair commit 014b17b changed BOTH the score mode and dedupe, but the controlled comparison shows the contributions are sharply asymmetric: essentially the entire gain comes from standardizing the score, not from dedupe. This closes the previously OPEN interaction question. NEGATIVE RESULT worth stating: even under the better score mode, dedupe is worth only +0.0065 recall@8, so the 2x2 does NOT support a strong 'dedupe only pays off after standardizing' claim. WITHDRAWN CLAIM: an earlier diagnostic (p2-index-duplication-confusion-2026-09-15, predicted q=0.3) attributed +0.1245 to dedupe; that arm toggled the distiller while shrinking the pool 353->177, and the same artifact's pool-size control shows pool size alone moves recall@8 by up to 0.25 at constant evidence survival, so the gain was confounded. FLOOR-CLEANLINESS OF THE 2x2, measured with the read-only probe eval/j5-floor-sensitivity-probe.ts (2 conversations, floor=0.02): the four 2x2 cells have gold-in-top8 misfire rate 0.0% and top-8 median scores far above the floor -- additive 0.5697 (dedupe) / 0.5876 (no dedupe), standardized 4.4758 / 5.1538 -- i.e. one to two orders of magnitude above floor=0.02, so all four cells are unaffected by the floor and ARE comparable to each other. THE SAME PROBE SHOWS RRF IS NOT FLOOR-CLEAN: with dedupe, 48.3% of top-8 candidates and 21.9% of gold-in-top8 sit at or below 0.02 (top-8 median 0.0202); WITHOUT dedupe it is far worse -- 79.6% of top-8 and 69.1% of gold-in-top8 misfired (median 0.0178). CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RRF ARMS: rrf-e2e 0.0745 and rrf-e2e-no-recency 0.0609 are floor-suppressed false negatives and MUST NOT be cited as evidence that RRF is poor end-to-end; measured under a non-suppressing shared criterion (standardized score over the pool, floor=0.02) they are 0.1536 and 0.1757. GENERAL RULE: any recall comparison ACROSS retrievalScoreMode is invalid if the hit criterion tests the arm OWN score against mem.config.retrievalFloor, because the three modes live in different score domains (additive ~O(0.5), standardized ~O(1-5), rrf ~O(0.01-0.04), rrf capped at weight-sum/(k+1) = 2.3/61 = 0.0377). Mechanism: src/locomo.ts:247 (`c.score > mem.config.retrievalFloor`) is domain-blind; j5-longmemeval-recall.ts shares it. Within-family (same score mode) comparisons, including the whole 2x2 above, are unaffected. Any cross-mode recall comparison must state which criterion was used. PROVENANCE WARNING: commit ad13751 stored 1-conversation/199-question SMOKE-TEST FRAGMENTS for the five per-arm decomp artifacts; commit ef5061b replaced them with the correct full 10-conversation/1986-question products. Only the full-run numbers are citable. CAUTION: these delivery-track figures are NOT comparable with j5-rrf-fusion-ablation (re-ranking diagnostic track, top-150 pool, no floor). Do not subtract across the two families.

j5-locomo-recall-longmemeval.notes: LongMemEval official cleaned variant, 500 questions, full run in 1007.6s. Source: the LongMemEval GitHub repo does NOT host data; the official release is on Hugging Face under MIT. longmemeval_s_cleaned.json = 277,383,467 bytes, sha256 d6f21ea9d60a0d56f34a05b609c79c88a451d2ae03597821ea3d5a9678c3a442. question_type distribution: multi-session 133 / temporal-reasoning 133 / knowledge-update 78 / single-session-user 70 / single-session-assistant 56 / single-session-preference 30; answer:null count = 0 (this variant has NO abstention questions). Metric convention as recorded in the artifact: granularity = session (one haystack session per episode, matching LongMemEval's official session-level convention); recall@K = the gold session (or its fact_ variant) appears in top-K AND score > retrievalFloor(0.02); nDCG here is BINARY relevance whereas LongMemEval official uses graded relevance, so the two are NOT the same quantity. RESULT: the DIRECTION replicates at all four K -- sim-only 0.9060 > no-recency 0.7560 > current 0.7300 at K=8. MAGNITUDE does not: the K=8 ratio is 1.24x versus 3.95x on LoCoMo, roughly one third. TWO CONFOUNDS that make the absolute values non-transferable between corpora: (1) GRANULARITY -- LongMemEval is session-level, LoCoMo is turn-level (dia_id), so the two recall values are two different rulers and must never be subtracted or compared directly. (2) POOL SIZE -- LongMemEval pools are 40-60 items so a top-150 truncation is a no-op, whereas LoCoMo pools average ~1176. Rank-fusion spread 1/(k+rank) therefore spans only ~1.8x on small pools versus ~20x on large ones, so an RRF-vs-sim-only comparison on LongMemEval may be a pool-size artifact rather than a property of the fusion rule. KNOWN DEFECT in eval/j5-longmemeval-recall.ts scoreOne() (line ~119): it applies c.score > floor per arm, which invalidates any fourth RRF arm (the score-domain incompatibility documented in j5-e2e-causal-decomposition). Must be changed to a common floor criterion before adding an RRF arm.

j5-rrf-floor-control.notes: LoCoMo 10 conversations, 1986 questions, NO_GATING, corpus sha256 79fa87e9...98ff4, dedupe ON, poolSizeMean 600.6. PURPOSE: settle whether the low end-to-end RRF recall reported by j5-e2e-causal-decomposition (rrf-e2e 0.0745 / rrf-e2e-no-recency 0.0609) is a real ranking-capability gap or an artifact of the hit criterion. Three criteria x four arms, same run: (A) rank-only (score-blind, ADOPTED), (B) shared store-standardized score vs floor, (C) each arm's own score vs floor (reproduces the contaminated condition). RESULT: contamination is real and quantified - criterion (C) kills 166/316 (rrf) and 240/363 (rrf-norec) top-8 gold candidates and understates recall@8 by 0.0791 / 0.1148, while killing 0 for standardized and additive. RRF weight sum is 2.30 (affect deliberately excluded from RRF_COMPONENTS; src/retrieval.ts:292), so the theoretical max is 2.30/61 = 0.03770; measured domain 0.00495-0.03449, median 0.00869 - the default floor 0.02 sits INSIDE it and only 1.9% (0.7% corrected) of the window passes. BUT the qualitative conclusion survives correction: under (A)/(B) rrf 0.1536 vs standardized 0.2064 = -0.0529, rrf-norec 0.1757 = -0.0307. Contamination had swallowed ~60% of the gap. Ranking-capability ordering standardized (0.2064) > rrf (0.1536) > additive (0.0821), consistent with track A. NOTE the previously cited 0.0745 / 0.0609 are floor-induced FALSE NEGATIVES and must not be used as evidence that RRF is poor end-to-end. ACCEPTANCE CRITERION MET: within track B the rrf vs rrf-norec ordering flips with the criterion (+0.0222 rank-only vs -0.0136 own-score), and track A (shared storeScore) agrees with the rank-only sign (+0.0579) - so the pre-registered falsifiable prediction held. Criterion (A) and (B) are bit-identical on all three fused arms (0 killed), which cross-validates two independent code paths; the single exception is additive under (B) (-0.0070, 14/166), which does not affect any conclusion. Honest boundary: (A) with retrievalFloor=0 is not the same thing in general; they coincide here only because 0 top-8 scores were non-positive - the script implements (A) as pure ranking and does not rely on that coincidence. Harness: fused-path topK prefix invariance asserted 132 times (guards against K-dependent re-ranking silently distorting R@1/2/4); criterion (C) reproduces 0.0745/0.0609/0.2064 bit-exactly against the earlier run.log, confirming same-caliber reproduction.

j5-aggregation-caliber.name: J5: macro vs micro aggregation caliber on one identical set of hits (closes the 0.1985 vs 0.2064 gap)

conditions.name: standardized-store-default
conditions.description: LoCoMo 10 conversations, 1986 questions, NO_GATING, dedupe ON, store default standardized scoring; the same hit set summarized under both calibers

j5-aggregation-caliber.notes: WHY: 0.1985 (09-19 artifacts) and 0.2064 (j5-rrf-e2e-decomposition) were long treated as needing a salienceSource explanation. That hypothesis is FALSIFIED - see j5-salience-source-repro. ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE: aggregation caliber. The 10 conversations carry UNEQUAL question counts (199/105/193/260/242/158/190/239/196/204 = 1986), so macro (per-conversation proportion, then mean over conversations; p2-quantile-retention-sweep.ts:172) and micro (per-question 0/1 pooled, then divide by total; j5-rrf-e2e-decomposition.ts:207) differ. CLOSED AT FULL PRECISION: same 410 hits at recall@8 give macro 0.19853236649084932 (bit-equal to the 09-19 figure 0.198532) and micro 0.20644511581067473 (bit-equal to store-default 0.206445); delta = +0.007912749319825413 equals micro-macro exactly. The two figures come from TWO DIFFERENT scripts over the SAME hit set - only the denominator differs. ⚠️ CONSEQUENCE: any difference taken ACROSS tracks or calibers is invalid; 0.1985 and 0.2064 must never be subtracted or juxtaposed. WHY THE OLD CROSS-CHECK MISSED IT: j5-rrf-e2e-decomposition.ts:224 compares measure() against avg(convHit) WITHIN one conversation, where covered/qa.length and mean(0/1) share the same denominator - it is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of detecting a cross-conversation aggregation difference, so its 0.000000 is not evidence.

j5-salience-source-repro.name: J5: falsification test for the salienceSource hypothesis behind 0.1985 vs 0.2064

conditions.name: pred-salience
conditions.description: injects p2-quantile-style salienceOf as salienceOverride

conditions.name: default-salience
conditions.description: no injection; store default branch

j5-salience-source-repro.notes: PURPOSE: test whether the 0.1985 vs 0.2064 gap is caused by the salience SOURCE (oracle/predicted). RESULT: hypothesis FALSIFIED, twice over. (1) Two arms differing ONLY in salience source, with scoreMode/dedupeByContent/retrievalFloor/weights asserted field-by-field identical (10/10 asserts passed), return the SAME recall@8: pred-salience 0.198532 (bit-reproducing the 09-19 figure) AND default-salience 0.198532 (NOT reproducing store-default 0.206445, delta -0.007913). (2) Mechanism: the two arms' episode.encoding.salience differ on 0 of 5882 episodes. CODE-LEVEL REASON: src/store.ts:254-256 - when salienceOverride is undefined the default branch IS clamp01(sigmoid(predictSalienceV2(content, ctx))), i.e. the SAME formula with the SAME ctx that p2-quantile's injection evaluates, so injecting predicted salience is a NO-OP. Consequence: the residual gap is fully explained by aggregation caliber (see j5-aggregation-caliber), and src/ default configuration has not changed since 09-19 (380dc2f / 55d692a are opt-in, c420ff2 default-off), so both figures stand. Also corrects an earlier belief: the 0.1985 and 0.2064 figures did NOT come from the same script and arm - they came from two different scripts (p2-quantile vs j5-rrf-e2e-decomposition), with identical poolSize 1176.4.
